| [ADCC, ADCP and CDC: antibody-guided effector mechanisms](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antibodies-and-b-cells/adcc-adcp-cdc) | An earlier macrophage contact is contrasted with a whole antibody-coated target and its nucleus inside a closed phagosome; the macrophage nucleus remains outside that inner compartment, and internalization is conditional. | `antibody-coating-adcp-v1-light.png` | Present | Present |

views.observation: Both cells stay external; the membrane-attached NK receptor meets outward Fc, the Fab tips face antigen, granule release is conditional and target death remains a question.
External contact and whole-target enclosure are distinct. The closed phagosome contains target, target nucleus and coating; the macrophage nucleus stays outside it.

Deposition and a pore spanning two leaflets are separate, with extracellular/cytosol labels and a lysis question. The target drawing itself is clipped by the left canvas edge in both themes; the whole source canvas was viewed.
Separate tissue arrangements show mixed cells, T/B regions and a labelled germinal center. The parent caption denies a required developmental path and specifies study-dependent criteria.

Matched tips, selected effector contacts and FcRn questions are distinct. The lower receptor icon lies close to the antibody arm; exact inset geometry needs source inspection before any binding-site claim.

Two heavy/four-domain and two light/two-domain chains are depicted. Fab includes variable and constant domains and Fc is labelled CH2/CH3. CL/CH1 outlines crowd one another but the text remains readable at native size.
